source: NCERT Class XII, Introductory Microeconomics, Ch. 5 (Market Equilibrium).

sections.heading: 1. Market Equilibrium
points: **Market equilibrium** occurs where **quantity demanded = quantity supplied** (the demand and supply curves intersect).
This determines the **equilibrium price** and **equilibrium quantity**.
At a price above equilibrium → **surplus (excess supply)** → price falls; below → **shortage (excess demand)** → price rises.

sections.heading: 2. Shifts in Demand and Supply
points: A **shift in demand** (due to income, tastes, prices of related goods): a rightward shift raises both equilibrium price and quantity; leftward lowers both.
A **shift in supply** (due to input costs, technology, etc.): a rightward shift lowers price but raises quantity; leftward raises price, lowers quantity.
**Simultaneous shifts** — the net effect depends on the relative magnitude.

sections.heading: 3. Elasticity
points: **Price elasticity of demand** = % change in quantity demanded ÷ % change in price (measures responsiveness).
**Elastic (>1), inelastic (<1), unit elastic (=1), perfectly elastic (∞), perfectly inelastic (0)**.
Determinants: **availability of substitutes, necessity vs luxury, share of income, time**.

sections.heading: 4. Government Intervention — Price Controls
points: **Price ceiling** — a **maximum legal price** below equilibrium (e.g. rationing of essentials) → causes **shortages and black markets**.
**Price floor** — a **minimum legal price** above equilibrium (e.g. **Minimum Support Price (MSP)** for crops, minimum wages) → causes **surpluses**.
Governments use these to protect consumers or producers, but they create distortions.

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Equilibrium: demand = supply (determines price and quantity).
Excess supply (surplus) → price falls; excess demand (shortage) → price rises.
Demand shift right → price & quantity up; supply shift right → price down, quantity up.
Price elasticity of demand = %ΔQd ÷ %ΔP; elastic >1, inelastic <1.
Price ceiling (below eq.) → shortage; price floor/MSP (above eq.) → surplus.

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: **Equilibrium = where demand meets supply** (Qd = Qs).
A **price ceiling (below equilibrium) causes shortages**; a **price floor (above equilibrium) causes surpluses**.
**MSP is a price floor** (minimum price for farmers).
**Elastic demand = elasticity > 1** (very responsive to price).
